scope: a record of external attribution numbers this project cites, with the protocol each was produced under. It settles whether they can be placed beside ours; it does not re-measure them

entries.claim: Explicit-quote accuracy, current state of the art
entries.protocol: ModernBERT joint scoring with GOLD character mentions and the GOLD character list, at training and evaluation; 5-fold cross-validation at book level. The authors call the setting unrealistic and give a separate LitBank number with predicted coreference
entries.why: we supply a roster but no gold mention spans, so their setting resolves for free what ours must infer

entries.protocol: category prediction on Quote-Said-Person, no oracle, reported on 22% of their corpus
entries.why: we reproduced it directly - PR #372 measured .9899 on the same pattern in our own data, so this one transfers and did

entries.claim: Zero-shot GPT-3.5, described as a strong baseline
entries.protocol: generation, beaten by SIG by 9% overall
entries.why: no absolute figure is quoted in a form that can be placed beside ours; only the margin over it

entries.protocol: scored as extractive reading comprehension against annotated spans; a generative model is penalised for answering with a name rather than a span
entries.why: the number measures format agreement more than attribution, and is the clearest evidence that these figures cannot be ranked

entries.protocol: same paper, same model, same protocol, different corpus
entries.why: 60 points from the same model in the same paper; the corpus and its annotation decide the number as much as the method does

entries.protocol: generation, roster supplied, no gold mentions, alias-aware exact-name scoring

verdict: one external number transfers - Elson's .99, which we reproduced ourselves at .9899. The rest were produced under oracles or scoring formats we do not share and must not be quoted as targets
